title: Twelve at the Fourth, First by Ten
title_candidates: Twelve at the Fourth, First by Ten
The Fourth Hole Will See You Now
Williams Plays the Golf of His Life, Loses by Ten
theme: Catalunya handed out craters all four days — a 12, three 10s, a 9 and an 11 — and the Trophy went not to the tidiest man but to the one who absorbed the biggest hole in TEG history and kept filing 40-point rounds. The fourth hole is the thread: Patterson's 12 there in R1, Williams's 8 there in R2, Williams's 9 there in R3 (which handed over BOTH the Trophy and the Jacket on the same hole), and Mullin's 8 there in R4 as the Spoon changed hands for good.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck; the wreckage played straight-faced, the winner ribbed for how he got there
opening_hook: Open on Patterson standing on the 4th at the Tour course in R1, signing for a 12 (b04) — the worst hole of the entire TEG — then cut immediately to him lifting the Trophy 68 holes later by 10 shots, and ask how on earth those two facts belong to the same man.
foreshadow: Patterson's 12 at the 4th in R1 (b04) — the fourth hole is introduced early as the tournament's crime scene and keeps returning
Williams opens with the best gross round of his life, +12 at the Tour course (b12) — file the number, it will not save him
Neumann's R1: a brand-new Tour course-worst of 105 (cr02), built from a 12 and a 10 at SI 1 (b09, b17)
Mullin arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder with eight Jackets on the shelf (player_history) — the two halves of his game are about to go in opposite directions

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: John Patterson (172 pts, by 10 from Gregg Williams)
competitions.how: Williams led after R1 and R2, by a single point each time, while Patterson quietly banked 45 and 42 despite a 12 at the 4th (b04) and a 10 at the 15th (b18). The tournament turned on two holes of R3 at the Stadium: Williams took the outright lead at the 3rd (b13), then made a 9 at the 4th (b20) and Patterson walked past him for good (b11). Patterson's 19 points across 12–17 (b07) turned a wobble into a 45-point round and an eight-point cushion; Williams's 11 at the 13th (b08) buried the argument. R4's 40 points, with 13 in the 3rd–6th stretch (b14), stretched it to 10 with no lead change in the final round at all.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Jon Baker (+63, by 8 from David Mullin)
competitions.how: Baker took a share of the gross lead late in R1 and held it for 23 holes into R3 (b01) before Williams — playing the best gross golf of his career — nudged ahead at the 3rd. He held it for precisely one hole: Baker was back in front at the 4th (b10) and never lost it again, converting a five-shot lead after R3 into eight by the finish. The exclamation mark came in R4: 89 gross at the Stadium, a new course record beating the 90 that had stood across 15 prior visits (cr01), and his own personal best on the course. Mullin's +64-ish gross golf was good enough for second and nothing else.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (139 pts) — a second consecutive Spoon
competitions.how: Alex Baker occupied the bottom place after R1, R2 and R3 and spent much of the Stadium round swapping it with Mullin hole by hole (b32, b33, b34, b35). Mullin's 30-point R3 left him one slip from the floor, and the slip came three holes into R4: a 9 at the 3rd (b28) dropped him to the bottom for good (b21), followed immediately by an 8 at the 4th — ten shots bled in three holes (b42). His 14 points across 11–14 (b15) was a fine piece of golf arriving roughly two hours too late; Alex Baker meanwhile posted a course PB 93 and escaped. Mullin therefore finished runner-up for the Jacket and dead last on the Trophy — normal handicapping, brutal timing.

rounds.chosen_headline: Patterson Makes a 12 and Still Signs for 45
rounds.angle: The fourth hole claims Patterson (b04) — the worst hole of the whole TEG — and he answers with 19 points in five holes (b06); at the other end Neumann posts a brand-new Tour course-worst 105 (cr02) while Williams quietly plays the gross round of his life (b12).

headline_candidates: Two Rounds, One Point, No Clarity
rounds.chosen_headline: Two Rounds, One Point, No Clarity
rounds.angle: Williams still leads by a single point on both metrics after Patterson's 10 at the 15th (b18) and Williams's own 8 at the 4th (b27) cancel each other out; the fourth hole quietly collects its second victim and Mullin sets a Tour course PB of 84 that will look ironic by Sunday.

headline_candidates: The Fourth Hole Decides Both Competitions
Twenty-Three Holes in Front, One Hole Behind
rounds.chosen_headline: The Fourth Hole Decides Both Competitions
rounds.angle: Act two's confrontation at the Stadium: Williams leads both competitions at the 3rd (b13, b01), then makes a 9 at the 4th and loses both on the same hole (b11, b10); an 11 at the 13th (b08) ends him, while Patterson survives a 10 and a 9 of his own and grinds out 19 points across 12–17 (b07) for a course PB 95.

headline_candidates: Baker Sets the Record, Mullin Takes the Spoon
89 at the Stadium, 9 at the Third
No Lead Changes, Plenty of Casualties
rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Sets the Record, Mullin Takes the Spoon
rounds.angle: Resolution: not a single lead change all round — Patterson closes with 40 for a 10-point win (b02), Jon Baker breaks the Stadium course record with 89 (cr01, b03), Mullin's 9 at the 3rd and 8 at the 4th hand him back-to-back Spoons (b28, b21, b42, b22), and Neumann's eagle at the easiest hole on the course (b05, b23) completes his journey from course-worst to course PB.

players.arc: Spoon-holder in TEG 10, fourth in TEG 11, and now Trophy winner by 10 — a second Trophy assembled around the biggest single-hole disaster in TEG history, a 12 at the 4th, plus a 10, another 10 and a 9 for good measure.

Played the best gross golf of his life — personal-best round (+12) and personal-best total (+76), new PBs on both Catalunya courses — led the Trophy for two rounds, and lost it in the space of eleven holes on Saturday to a 9 at the 4th and an 11 at the 13th: three prior Trophies, still no Jacket, and runner-up by ten.

The defending Trophy champion could not repeat, so he took the other prize instead: 23 holes in front on gross, one hole behind, then a wire-to-wire second half capped by a Stadium course record 89 and a second Green Jacket.

Eight Jackets and reigning Spoon holder, and both facts held true again — second on gross, last on Stableford, undone by a 9 at the 3rd and an 8 at the 4th within twenty minutes of the final round starting.

Opened with a 105 that is now the worst gross round ever recorded on the Tour course, closed with an eagle at the 15th and a Stadium personal best of 96 — and, for the first time in a while, walked away without the Spoon.

The TEG 10 champion sat at the bottom of the Spoon race after all three of the first rounds, then produced a 93 at the Stadium — a course PB by seven, thirteen better than his last visit — and was rescued by Mullin's third hole on Sunday.

cuts: b06 is colour, keep only as a one-liner
venue_notes: TEG's 3rd visit to Catalonia, and by now the resort is family: the Tour course took R1 and R2 (the 3rd and 4th TEG rounds there), the Stadium — Spain's premier course, European Tour design — took R3 and R4 (the 4th and 5th). Play the two-course split as a change of gear: the Tour course is the 'slightly more forgiving sibling' and it still produced a 12, two 10s and the worst round in its TEG history; the Stadium then decided all three competitions. Use the record beats as written (cr01's prior record of 90 had stood across 15 prior visits; cr02's prior worst of 103 across 10) — don't recompute visit numbers.
course_history_notes: Jon Baker's 89 in R4 is both a new Stadium course record (cr01) and his own personal best there, beating his 90 from TEG 11 by one.

Gregg Williams set personal bests on both courses — 84 at the Tour in R1 (8 better than his TEG 6 mark, and 8 better than his last visit) and 92 at the Stadium in R4 (7 better) — the best golf of his TEG life, for a runner-up medal.
Stuart Neumann's week in miniature: a new Tour course-worst 105 in R1, then a Stadium personal best of 96 in R4, four better than his TEG 6 visit.
Alex Baker's 93 at the Stadium in R4 was a course PB by 7 and 13 shots better than his last visit; John Patterson set course PBs at both venues (96 at the Tour in R1, 95 at the Stadium in R3).
David Mullin's R2 84 was a Tour course PB by one — the only line of his card he will want quoted.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R3 H4 at the Stadium — Williams makes 9, Patterson takes the outright lead (b20, b11) and is never headed across the final 32 holes, winning by 10.

Green Jacket: R3 H4 at the Stadium — one hole after losing a 23-hole grip on the gross lead (b01), Jon Baker takes it straight back (b10) and converts it into an 8-shot win, sealed with the record 89 (cr01).
Wooden Spoon: R4 H3 — Mullin's 9 (b28) drops him to the bottom for good (b21), three holes into the final round, after Alex Baker had owned the place for the previous three rounds.

payoffs.seed: Patterson's 12 at the 4th in R1 (b04) — the fourth hole as crime scene
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 3 and 'How the three were decided'
payoffs.payoff: The 4th returns in every round: Williams's 8 there in R2 (b27), his 9 there in R3 which hands over both the Trophy (b11) and the Jacket (b10) on the same hole, and Mullin's 8 there in R4 as the Spoon settles.

payoffs.seed: Williams's personal-best gross round of +12 in R1 (b12)
payoffs.payoff: It becomes a personal-best gross TOTAL of +76 (b16) — and still no Jacket, no Trophy, beaten by 10 and by 8 respectively; the best golf of his career filed under runner-up.

payoffs.seed: Neumann's new Tour course-worst 105 in R1 (cr02), built on a 12 and a 10 at SI 1
payoffs.payoff: He eagles the par-5 15th at the Stadium (b05 — the field's only eagle, b23), posts a course PB 96, and finishes above the Spoon line despite two prior Spoons and the Spoon in 2 of the last 3 TEGs.

payoffs.seed: Mullin: reigning Spoon holder with eight Jackets
payoffs.payoff: Both halves come true at once — second on gross behind Jon Baker (b03) and last on Stableford with 139 (b22), a second Spoon in a row decided by three holes on Sunday morning.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Baker's one-hole loss of the gross lead (b01) and his failure to retain the Trophy are real but minor — he still won the Jacket and set the course record; the week belongs to Patterson winning by 10 out of a crater field, so redemption_arc plus a catalogue of blow-ups leads, with Williams's R3 collapse as the tragic strand.
